newsitem.title: CHINA: ABB to invest $400 mln in China.
newsitem.headline: ABB to invest $400 mln in China.

text.p: Swiss-Swedish group ABB AB plans to invest $400 million in China over the next five years in addition to the $600 million already committed, president Percy Barnevik said on Wednesday.

ABB will invest in a number of factories that will supply equipment for the massive Three Gorges dam project in central Hubei province and western Sichuan, compay officials told reporters without giving details.
Barnevik said the engineering group already had 18 joint ventures in China but declined to say whether operations overall were profitable.
"They range from very profitable to big loss-makers," he said.
"Typically it takes two to three years to turn a profit though sometimes it is four or five," he said.

An electrical switchgear plant in the southeastern city of Xiamen was among the money-makers while a power transformer operation in Hefei in the eastern province of Anhui had not made a profit after two to three years of operation, he said.
China represented 3-4 percent of the group's worldwide business now but that would rise to 10 percent over 10 to 15 years, according to Barnevik.
He said $500 million to $1 billion of orders in large projects were in the pipeline, though he could not say when they would be booked.
